messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and at a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Helps | |------|------------|--------------| | **1. Clean & Inspect** | Give it a gentle wipe‑down, check for cracks, loose screws, or other damage. | A clean, well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows you’re honest about its condition. | | **2. Take Quality Photos** | Use natural light, capture front, back, neck, headstock, soundhole, and any flaws. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce questions later. | | **3. Write a Clear Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, wood type, finish, any upgrades, and a brief history. | Transparency builds trust and speeds up negotiations. | | **4. Set a Realistic Price** | Research similar listings on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music stores. | Competitive pricing attracts offers while still giving you room to negotiate. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Online Marketplaces** – Reverb (music‑specific), eBay, Etsy (if vintage).
• **Local Classifieds** – Craigslist, Gumtree, Nextdoor.
• **Social Media Groups** – Facebook Marketplace, local buy/sell groups, Reddit r/GuitarSwap.
• **Consignment Shops** – Local music stores often take a commission but handle shipping and paperwork. | Multiple platforms increase visibility; choose what fits your comfort level with shipping vs. local pickup. | | **6. Decide on Shipping vs. Pickup** | • **Pickup** – Saves money, no shipping risk.
• **Shipping** – Use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and trackable insurance. | Shipping can widen your buyer pool but adds cost and risk; pick what matches your budget and time. | | **7. Negotiate Safely** | Keep all communication within the platform’s messaging system if possible. For cash deals, meet in a public place or store lobby. | Protects against scams and ensures you have a record of agreements. | | **8. Finalize the Sale** | Once you accept an offer, confirm payment method (bank transfer, PayPal, Venmo, cash). Provide a receipt or bill of sale. | Documentation protects both parties and clarifies ownership transfer. | | **9. Ship or Hand Over** | If shipping, use a reputable courier, insure the package, and share tracking info. If local, hand over keys, original accessories, and any documentation. | Proper delivery reduces disputes and keeps the buyer satisfied. | ### Quick Tips - **Price Flexibility:** Start slightly above your target price to allow room for negotiation. - **Highlight Unique Features:** If you’ve added custom pickups, a new fretboard, or a special finish, mention them—they can justify a higher price. - **Use “For Sale” Tags:** On Facebook Marketplace, add tags like “Acoustic Guitar,” “Used,” “Good Condition.” - **Respond Promptly:** Buyers appreciate quick replies—this can lead to faster sales. ### Example Listing Title & Description ``` Title: 2010 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition – $250 Description: - Brand/Model: Yamaha FG800 - Year: 2010 - Wood: Spruce top, Nato back & sides - Finish: Natural - Condition: Light play marks, no cracks, fully functional - Extras: Original case, extra strings, cleaning kit - Serial #: 12345678 - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a larger instrument - Asking: $250 (negotiable) ``` Feel free to adapt this template to match your guitar’s specifics. Good luck with your sale!
